title: Session Secrets Leaked via Tool Call Arguments

invariant.statement: Session secrets (API keys, OAuth tokens, signed credentials, refresh tokens) must never appear verbatim in the argument JSON of a tool call. Tools must reference secrets by an opaque server-side handle that the dispatcher dereferences before invocation.

claim.statement: If session secrets appear in tool call argument JSON, they will land in observability sinks (request logs, distributed traces, error reports, audit trails, third-party LLM provider transcripts) where the threat surface is far broader than the agent runtime. A read of any of those sinks — including by anyone with access to the tracing system — yields the secrets.

mitigation.summary: Secrets live in a server-side capability vault. Tools receive an opaque handle (capability:abc123) in their args. The dispatcher dereferences handles immediately before invoking the tool implementation; the dereferenced secret never crosses the trace/log boundary. Loggers redact handle dereferences. The LLM context never contains a raw secret; it sees only handles.

references: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
